teaser.text: Cintas is a workplace-services company: it keeps employees dressed, premises clean, and safety systems ready. Its dollar comes in through recurring service work and goes out through merchandise, people, processing, vehicles, and the overhead required to deliver it.

stock.title: Cintas stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Cintas stock forecast: the weighted scenario, cash generation, valuation, and UniFirst risks shaping the range.
stock.opening: The weighted price reaches $220.12 in October 2029, after $209.88 in October 2027 and $211.43 in October 2028. It hinges on FTC clearance, financing, and UniFirst integration.
stock.closing: The full memo also covers Cintas's business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Cintas's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: Cintas’s probability-weighted outcome is close to flat at first, then improves modestly. The weighted price is $209.88 in October 2027, against today’s $213.06. It reaches $211.43 in October 2028 and $220.12 in October 2029, producing returns of negative 1%, positive 1% and positive 7%, including dividends.
By October 2029, the forecast spans $148.21 in the bear case to $320.08 in the bull case. The width reflects unresolved FTC, financing and integration risks.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Cintas?

paragraphs.text: The base case assumes $14,000 million of revenue initially, then $15,000 million and $16,000 million, with margins recovering from 16.7857% to 17.625%. The bear case holds earnings near $2,250 million to $2,350 million as growth slows and synergies fail to appear. The bull case reaches $3,200 million as 8.9% organic growth, denser routes and plant efficiencies combine.

The bear case assumes delay, remedies or failure around UniFirst, weaker standalone growth and limited buybacks. Lower earnings and a fall toward 25x outweigh dividends, taking the shares from $170.03 in October 2027 to $148.21 in October 2029. Its probability is 28% because the acquisition combines regulatory, financing, dilution and execution risks, although Cintas’s core earnings record prevents this from becoming the central case.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Cintas really make?

paragraphs.text: Net income was $1,999,968 thousand in fiscal 2026. Operating cash flow was $2,276,280 thousand. After $395,105 thousand of capital spending, free cash flow was $1,881,175 thousand. That is strong conversion, although free-cash-flow growth lagged earnings.

blocks.heading: How much does Cintas pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Dividends remain supportive. The base case moves from $2.08 per share in October 2027 to $2.33 in October 2028 and $2.61 in October 2029. The bear case applies 5% growth; the bull applies 15%. Cintas has raised DPS from $0.95 in 2022 to $1.80 in 2026, while fiscal 2026 free cash flow of $1,881.175 million exceeded dividends of $701.485 million.

blocks.heading: Does Cintas's dividend come from free cash flow?

paragraphs.text: From May 2022 to May 2026, free cash flow rose from 1,296,953 to 1,881,175 in US$ thousands. In fiscal 2026, dividends and buybacks returned 1,653,589, or 87.9% of free cash flow, leaving cash for acquisitions and investments. The table shows how those uses and financing sources fit together across five years.

Net income was $1,999,968 thousand in fiscal 2026. Operating cash flow was $2,276,280 thousand. After $395,105 thousand of capital spending, free cash flow was $1,881,175 thousand. That is strong conversion, although free-cash-flow growth lagged earnings.

blocks.heading: What has Cintas guided for fiscal 2027?

paragraphs.text: Management’s guidance—its forecast rather than a guarantee—now calls for fiscal 2027 revenue of $12,150.0–$12,270.0 million and adjusted diluted EPS of $5.45–$5.54. The forecast implies revenue growth of 7.9%–8.9%. Cintas raised it on September 23, 2026, for the year ending in May 2027.

blocks.heading: Did Cintas keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Cintas also exceeded its original fiscal 2026 forecast. Management had projected revenue of US$11.00–11.15 billion and diluted EPS of US$4.71–4.85. It delivered US$11.26 billion and reported EPS of US$4.91. That supports confidence in execution, but not necessarily in every investment.

blocks.heading: What do Cintas's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue reached $3,013,981 thousand, up 10.9% from the prior-year quarter. Acquisitions added 0.4 percentage points, while one extra working day added 1.7 points. After those effects and currency, organic growth was 8.9%. Rental grew organically by 8.0%, and First Aid grew by 14.2%.

Net income rose to $551,711 thousand, while EPS reached $1.36. Tax moved against the comparison because discrete items, chiefly stock compensation, affected both periods. That explains why net income grew more slowly than operating profit.

blocks.heading: What should Cintas watch in the next release?

paragraphs.text: The next operating checkpoint is the quarter ending November 30, 2026, followed by the February and May quarters. Those results will show whether the first-quarter beat persists. If the deal closes, Cintas must explain the new earnings, interest expense, shares, integration costs and the $350 million reverse termination fee payable in specified antitrust-blocking circumstances.
